Subject: Azure private plan: co-sell & revenue split

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the intro via Eliot. Novus Health is interested in listing Redwood on the Azure Private Offers program with co-sell enabled. Procurement asked me to get a clear picture on:

- Proposed revenue split / payout schedule for Azure co-sell (is Redwood the merchant of record or will you list as a third-party with Microsoft routing?).
- Required evidence for entitlements (SOC2, data residency attestations, any marketplace-specific proofs).
- Invoicing cadence and whether Azure invoice routing will suffice for our internal AR.

I've attached a short SOW template that our legal team would use as a starting point (see attachment stub: Novus_SOW_request_template.pdf). Can you and your team confirm what you need from us to proceed?

We'd like to move quickly—can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to align?

Best,
Samira

Novus Health

Hi Samira — thanks, and hello Eliot.

High level answers up front:

- Revenue split: Redwood typically supports the Azure co-sell payout schedule and can operate as either merchant of record (MoR) or as a seller who accepts Azure routing depending on the customer's procurement requirements. For Novus-sized deals we commonly recommend Azure routing + a 70/30 net split (example in attached COSell_Revenue_Schedule.xlsx).
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II report, summary of data residency/config (we can provide region-scoped runtime attestations), and a short audit-logs extract for the pilot period.
- Invoicing: Azure invoice routing is acceptable to most customers; we can also provide vendor invoices if Novus requires them.

I've attached a proposed revenue schedule and a draft SOW link (stub) to accelerate legal review. Jordan and Marissa are looped for billing / legal redlines.

Available for a quick 30-minute sync today between 3:00–4:30pm PT or tomorrow morning. Which works best?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Hi — attaching the SOC2 summary and a short note on audit logs and residency options (attachment stub: SOC2-evidence-summary.zip). A few clarifications:

- We can provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report and a one-page control summary. For audit logs, we can supply token-level request traces for the pilot window; full raw logs require an NDA specific to log access.
- Data residency: Redwood will pin the tenant to the Azure region you select (eastus / centralus options available). We will document the region in the SOW.
- Payment terms: Redwood standard is 30 days net for direct vendor invoices. If you go with Azure routing and payouts, the timing follows Azure's settlement cadence — usually monthly with a ~45–60 day lag depending on settlement. We can offer 30 days net only if Redwood invoices Novus directly (MoR).

I've also added a short exemplar billing flow in the email body:
- Path A (Azure routing): Novus subscribes via Azure Private Offer -> Azure bills Novus -> Microsoft remits to Redwood per co-sell schedule -> Redwood reconciles.  (recommended for co-sell benefits)
- Path B (Redwood MoR): Novus signs Redwood SOW, Redwood invoices monthly -> Novus pays Redwood -> Redwood reports to Microsoft for co-sell crediting as applicable.

If this sounds ok, let's lock a 30-minute call on Fri 20 Jun at 10:00am PT. I'll include Jordan to walk through the billing diagram live.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

- Procurement prefers Redwood to accept 45-day payment timing if we go via Azure settlement (we understand there may be a lag). If you can invoice directly as MoR for the pilot, we could accept 30 days net.
